title.en: Woman assaulted after Travelodge staff gave room key to her abuser
title.zh: Travelodge员工将房间钥匙交给施虐者后，一女子遭到袭击

summary.en: A woman seeking refuge from domestic abuse was physically attacked after Travelodge staff mistakenly gave her room key to her abuser. This incident highlights a pattern of the hotel chain providing keys to men without proper verification.
summary.zh: 一名寻求摆脱家庭暴力的女性在入住Travelodge酒店后遭到人身攻击，原因是酒店员工错误地将她的房间钥匙交给了施虐者。这起事件凸显了该连锁酒店在未经验证的情况下将钥匙交给男性的惯常做法。

body.en: The woman had gone to London hotel for a ‘night away from the fear’ in latest incident of chain giving keys to men without checking first Travelodge staff gave a room key to the domestic abuser of a woman, who then physically attacked her. The woman, who is remaining anonymous, told the BBC that she was staying in a branch of the hotel in London to escape the man, but he followed her and was given a key by the reception staff. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这名女子前往伦敦酒店度过了一个“远离恐惧的夜晚”，最近发生了连锁酒店在未事先检查的情况下将钥匙交给男性的事件。Travelodge的工作人员将房间钥匙交给了一名妇女的家庭虐待者，然后该妇女对她进行了身体攻击。这名不愿透露姓名的女子告诉英国广播公司，她当时住在伦敦一家酒店的分店，以躲避这名男子，但这名男子跟踪了她，接待人员给了一把钥匙。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This distressing incident underscores the profound vulnerability of those fleeing abuse and the critical need for safe havens. Yahweh calls us to actively defend the oppressed and seek justice for those who cannot protect themselves, reminding us of our collective responsibility to ensure safety and dignity for all.
reflection.zh: 这起令人痛心的事件凸显了那些逃离虐待者所面临的极度脆弱，以及对安全避难所的迫切需求。雅伟呼召我们积极捍卫受欺压者，为那些无法自保的人寻求公义，提醒我们有共同的责任确保所有人的安全和尊严。

verse.textEn: Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.
verse.textZh: 学习行善，寻求公平，解救受欺压的；给孤儿伸冤，为寡妇辨屈。

Yahweh's word cautions that those who live by violence often face its destructive return.
reflection.zh: 在冲突时期，使用武力往往导致暴力滋生更多苦难的循环。这则新闻提醒我们，当国家诉诸武力时，其后果会波及整个社会，影响企业和民生。雅伟的话语告诫我们，那些靠暴力生存的人，往往会面临其毁灭性的反噬。

summary.en: Reform says it will free up space in jails in England and Wales by rapidly deporting all foreign offenders Good morning. Andy Burnham has said Middlemarch is his favourite novel, but he may not remember George Eliot’s line about the genial businessman Mr Vincy who “blustering as...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Reform says it will free up space in jails in England and Wales by rapidly deporting all foreign offenders Good morning. Andy Burnham has said Middlemarch is his favourite novel , but he may not remember George Eliot’s line about the genial businessman Mr Vincy who “blustering as he was, had as little of his own way as if he had been a prime minister”. Burnham only took over in No 10 three weeks ago today. But already he is learning that Eliot had a point about the constraints of office. As PM, Burnham became responsible for the prisoner early release scheme due to come into force in September, which is hugely controversial because it will lead to killers, rapists and sex offenders being released early. Burnham immediately said he was “pausing” the scheme pending a rethink, and early last week he announced he was changing the rules to make the scheme more restrictive . Explaining the move in an article for the Daily Telegraph, Burnham said that he “wanted to go even further” but that the plan he was announcing “pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do.” He added: “I know I can look people in the eye and say to them there is nothing more I could have asked for without risking the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing within months.” Yusuf [says] Reform will deport “all 10,000 foreign nationals from our prisons.” Of the 10,134 foreign nationals in custody in England and Wales, nearly a third are on remand, i.e. they haven’t been convicted of a crime yet. A Reform official confirmed foreign nationals will only come in scope of the party’s scheme if and when they’re convicted. Then there are questions about what’d happen after inmates in Kosovo finish their sentence (Reform would put a lifetime ban on returning to the U.K.). Or matters like El Salvador’s human rights record — though Playbook can imagine how Farage will respond to that one. Keeping the public safe is and always will be Labour’s first priority. The government has already made clear we are working at pace to deport foreign criminals and we’re building more prison places to deliver justice for victims and keep criminals behind bars. Reform have no serious answers to the Tory prisons crisis and would lead the system to collapse. This would result in a free for all for dangerous and violent offenders, including murderers and rapists. Nigel Farage and Reform simply can’t be trusted to keep Britain safe. Continue reading...
body.zh: 改革表示，它将通过迅速驱逐所有外国罪犯来释放英格兰和威尔士监狱的空间。早上好。安迪·伯纳姆曾说过《米德尔马契》是他最喜欢的小说，但他可能不记得乔治·艾略特关于文西先生的和蔼可亲的商人的台词，文西先生“尽管他很咆哮，但几乎没有我行我素，就好像他是一名首相一样”。伯纳姆三周前的今天才接任第十位。但他已经了解到艾略特关于办公室限制的观点是有道理的。作为总理，伯纳姆负责将于 9 月生效的囚犯提前释放计划，该计划引起很大争议，因为它将导致杀手、强奸犯和性犯罪者提前释放。伯纳姆立即表示，他正在“暂停”该计划，等待重新考虑，并于上周早些时候宣布，他正在更改规则，以使该计划更具限制性。伯纳姆在《每日电讯报》的一篇文章中解释这一举措时表示，他“想走得更远”，但他宣布的计划“已经达到了可能做到的极限”。他补充道：“我知道我可以看着人们的眼睛，对他们说，如果不冒着监狱系统达到极限并在几个月内崩溃的风险，我已经没有什么可以要求的了。”优素福[说]改革将“将所有10,000名外国人驱逐出我们的监狱”。在英格兰和威尔士被拘留的 10,134 名外国人中，近三分之一处于还押状态，即他们尚未被定罪。一名改革官员证实，外国人只有在被定罪后才会纳入该党计划的范围。然后还有关于科索沃囚犯刑满后会发生什么的问题（改革将终身禁止返回英国）。或者像萨尔瓦多的人权记录这样的事情——尽管 Playbook 可以想象法拉奇将如何回应这一问题。保证公众安全是而且永远是工党的首要任务。政府已经明确表示，我们正在加紧努力驱逐外国罪犯，我们正在建造更多监狱，为受害者伸张正义，并将罪犯关进监狱。改革对保守党监狱危机没有任何严肃的答案，并且会导致该体系崩溃。这将使包括杀人犯和强奸犯在内的所有危险和暴力犯罪者都获得自由。根本不能相信奈杰尔·法拉奇和改革能保证英国的安全。继续阅读...

title.en: Thailand: Gunshots fired in government office, ex-MP arrested
title.zh: 泰国：政府办公室发生枪击，前议员被捕

summary.en: A former lawmaker was arrested in Thailand after allegedly firing several shots at a senior official in a government office. This incident occurred just days after the country experienced its deadliest shooting in nearly four years.
summary.zh: 泰国一名前议员因涉嫌在政府办公室向一名高级官员开枪而被捕。这起事件发生在泰国近四年来最致命的枪击案几天之后。

body.en:
The suspected shooter is reportedly a former lawmaker who fired several shots at a senior official at a government office. The incident came just days after Thailand's deadliest shooting in nearly four years.

Thai Police arrested a suspected gunman — a former lawmaker — after he allegedly fired shots at a local government office at the outskirts of Bangkok, on Monday morning.

The shooter fired shots at a senior provincial officer and his driver, Nonthaburi police chief Major Dejrapee Kongdee told Reuters news agency.

Meanwhile, the Bangkok Post reported that the provincial administration's president, Thongchai Yenprasert, had died in the shooting.

As per the report, the suspected shooter forced his way into the government office at about 11 a.m. local time (0400 GMT) and fired several shots at Thongchai. The official was given cardiopulmonary resuscitation at the scene befoe being rushed to a local hospital where he was declared dead.

This comes just days after a 14-year-old's shooting rampage, first at his home and then at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, left nine people dead and over 20 injured. That incident was Thailand's deadliest mass shooting in nearly four years.

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul had reiterated his intention to tighten gun control laws in the wake of the shooting. The southeast Asian country's current gun laws do not include mental health screenings and allows people as young as 20 to hold guns.

Thailand had around 15 guns per 100 ⁠residents, the highest rate in Southeast Asia ​by a wide margin, according to a 2017 estimate by the Small Arms Survey.

title.en: China evacuates one million from homes as massive storm arrives
title.zh: 特大风暴袭来，中国数百万人撤离家园

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall, bringing strong winds and heavy rain across eastern China including Shanghai.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Chinese authorities have evacuated more than a million people from their homes in eastern China including the financial capital Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall.

The typhoon brought heavy rain and halted transportation across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai alone on Monday.

While authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm, they continue to warn of torrential rains, severe flooding and the risk of landslides through to Wednesday as the storm moves north.

Chinese authorities had earlier issued their highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit China this year.

It packed maximum wind speeds of 150km/h (94mph) when it first slammed into Yuhuan in the Zhejiang province at 17:30 (09:30 GMT) on Sunday before making a second landfall in the city of Wenzhou about an hour later, meteorological authorities said.

Heavy rain was forecast on Monday for the provinces of Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and the city of Shanghai.

Governments have urged people to avoid outdoor activities, while several top tourist attractions remain closed, including parts of Disneyland and Legoland, and several viewing platforms along the Bund in Shanghai.

Footage on state media show ground-floor businesses flooded in the former French Concession in Shanghai, an area popular with tourists, and people wading through ankle-deep waters.

Several state media outlets have reported that a nine-year-old boy from Wenling, Zhejiang is missing after being swept into the sea. Chinese officials have not reported any casualties.

Parts of Zhejiang could receive 250mm to 500mm of rain over the next few days, forecasters say.

Authorities in Hangzhou, Zhejiang's capital city, have waived parking fees in all public spaces for drivers seeking shelter amid the strong winds and floodwaters.

Elsewhere in the province, Wenzhou authorities have relocated some 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters, while about 390,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in the city of Taizhou.

In the coastal province of Fujian, maritime authorities have suspended dozens of passenger ferry routes and halted more than 100 offshore construction projects.

The storm moved over a long distance of 6,000km before making landfall, suggesting a lifespan of more than three times that of an average typhoon, according to China's state broadcaster CCTV.

It also has a massive circulation size and intense rainfall capacity, CCTV reported.

Misinformation around the storm has apparently spread rapidly on the Chinese internet, with state media reporting that two people have been detained for distributing such content.

title.en: When extreme heat threatens Europe's nuclear power
title.zh: 当极端高温威胁欧洲核电时

summary.en: Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.
summary.zh: 欧洲各地，河流变暖和水位下降正迫使核电站减少发电量。虽然全年来看损失微乎其微，但在关键时期，电力损失会对电网和电价产生影响。

body.en:
Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.

The state of the Danube is currently showing just how dependent nuclear power plants are on their local conditions . At the power station in Paks, Hungary — which normally produces about 40% of the country's electricity needs — only one of four turbine units is still operating. Due to record-low water levels in the Danube, the country's only nuclear power plant was even briefly at risk of a complete shutdown.

But for the European electricity market, France is of far greater significance. No other country in Europe relies so heavily on nuclear power, and if output in France drops, the country supplies less electricity to its neighbors, and may even become an electricity importer itself.

Over the course of the entire year, heat-related production losses at French power plants are minimal, but during individual weeks of extreme heat , the restrictions can be significant.

A 2023 report by France's official audit office estimated that, between 2000 and 2022, annual losses across all of the country's nuclear reactors due to high water temperatures and low river levels amounted to less than 1% of annual nuclear power production in any given year. Even in the extremely hot summer of 2003, they amounted to only about 1.5%.

But the annual figures obscure short-term fluctuations. In the summer of 2003, French nuclear power plants had to temporarily reduce their output by more than six gigawatts, and the most recent heat waves at the end of June and in mid-July 2026 saw the maximum available capacity was temporarily limited by eight to nine gigawatts. This corresponds to up to one-fifth of the nuclear power capacity normally available to France in the summer.

But eight gigawatts less capacity is not the same as an eight gigawatt overall shortfall. Even without the low water levels, some reactors would not be running at full capacity — either because of lower summer demand, high solar-power production, or bottlenecks in the power grid. According to grid operators, France still had sufficient reserves even during the 2026 heat waves and, on balance, remained an electricity exporter.

Nevertheless, such restrictions are relevant for grid operators and electricity traders. For them, it doesn't matter how much electricity was ultimately produced by nuclear power plants at the end of the year: What is crucial for the stability of the power grids and short-term price surges is whether the power is actually available when it is needed.

title.en: 'Change the game': Ukraine's latest target sits at the centre of everyday Russian life
title.zh: “改变游戏规则”：乌克兰的最新目标位于俄罗斯日常生活的中心

summary.en: Experts note that Ukraine's drone strategy is evolving to target Russia's largest online retailer, indicating a shift in tactics to impact everyday Russian life.

body.en:
Ukraine is bringing the war home to Russia, experts say, with a growing campaign of long-range drone strikes targeting infrastructure embedded in everyday Russian life.

More than four years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Ukraine is increasingly using domestically produced drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory.

Among the targets is Wildberries, Russia's biggest online retailer, with a sprawling network of warehouses and distribution centres.

At least 20 Wildberries locations have been targeted , including sites more than 2,000km from Ukraine.

They say the attacks demonstrate Ukraine's expanding ability to reach deep inside Russia, while making the economic and psychological costs of the war harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

Professor Matthew Sussex, a defence and national security expert at Deakin University, said Ukraine is deliberately trying to make the war's consequences harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

"Ukraine is hitting Wildberries mainly to bring the cost of war home to Russians," he said.

He described Wildberries as Russia's version of Amazon, a platform where people can buy almost anything and have it delivered to their door.

"Wildberries has become extremely popular for everyday Russians to order things, consumer goods that they have relied on in the past which have become unavailable due to the sanctions regime [placed on Russia by other countries]," he said.

Sussex said Ukraine's strategy is ultimately about making Russians feel the consequences of a war that, for many, has remained at a distance.

"If you're in Moscow or some parts of St Petersburg, you don't really feel the cost of the conflict," he said.

Ukraine says Wildberries has been involved in supplying Russian forces with military and dual-use equipment.

Retired Australian Army major-general Mick Ryan agreed there's a strategic reason for choosing Wildberries.

"These things are part of the Russian military logistics network," he said. "Russian soldiers and units buy things out of these warehouses all the time."

Wildberries and the Russian government have both said the e-commerce giant does not supply to the army.

Sussex believes the broader economic impact is ultimately more significant. Wildberries has billions of dollars in annual sales, and thousands of Russian businesses rely on the platform to sell and distribute their products.

"The concern is that if these attacks continue, then Wildberries may have to be bailed out by the government," Sussex said.

title.en: The tiny island bracing for an Odyssey tourism boom — even though it wasn't in the film
title.zh: 小岛为“奥德赛”旅游热潮做准备，尽管它并未出现在电影中

summary.en: Locals on a small island anticipate a significant increase in tourism, driven by the mistaken belief that the island was featured in a popular film. However, some residents express disappointment that no scenes were actually filmed there.
summary.zh: 一个小岛的居民预计旅游业将大幅增长，因为人们误以为该岛曾出现在一部热门电影中。然而，一些居民对岛上并未拍摄任何场景感到失望。

body.en:
Standing on the ferry as it waits to dock on the Greek island of Ithaca, Giorgia Ongarato is only too keen to talk about the Odyssey — the epic poem that inspired Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film.

The Italian lawyer said it was her dream to come to Ithaca, widely believed to be the same island the poem's hero Odysseus called home.

Dressed in a T-shirt emblazoned with the word 'Odyssey' in ancient Greek alongside a line from the poem, she enthused: "I studied Greek when I was a child, and I studied the Odyssey."

While she stressed that the film was not her entry point into the tale of the hero battling his way back home from the Trojan war, the 50-year-old said she was also a fan of the film — describing it as "wonderful".

The island's businesses and officials now expect the film to inspire many more to follow in her footsteps.

Ithaca, in the Ionian Sea off the west coast of mainland Greece, is far from the country's tourist hubs, and despite crystal-clear waters and spectacular bays, it has never been a regular stop for travellers.

Its interior is rugged, carpeted with olive and cypress trees, and strikingly calm even at the height of the tourist season.

Although the movie has undoubtedly piqued the interest of many, it has also been slightly controversial in Greece — although some Greek locations were used, not a single scene in the blockbuster was shot on Ithaca.

That decision has upset some on the island of roughly 3,000 inhabitants, where the film has been shown twice in open-air screenings since its 16 July worldwide release.

Xhimi Xoxha, who runs a restaurant in Ithaca's capital of Vathi, said he was content that the movie was already "generating publicity for the island". He predicted the positive effects would continue.

While Ithaca mayor Dionysis Stanitsas agreed that the publicity was "tremendous", he could not hide his disappointment that the island itself did not feature.

"We had reached out to the production team and asked that some scenes be filmed here on the island," he said. "Unfortunately, that wasn't feasible."

He is, however, counting on rising demand next year, and the island was already fully booked for this season by the time the film came out.

"As more people see it, they will begin planning trips to visit the island," he said.

Visitors will not find a palace of Odysseus or any spectacular archaeological site likely to confirm the existence of the hero of Homer's poem.

But village squares and the town hall are dotted with statues of Odysseus and Homer.

title.en: Western Europe records hottest June and July on record
title.zh: 西欧录得有史以来最热的六月和七月

summary.en: Western Europe has experienced its hottest June and July on record, leading to widespread drought, unusually dry soils, and low river levels. Forecasters warn that a strengthening El Nino could further increase global temperatures later this year.
summary.zh: 西欧经历了有记录以来最热的六月和七月，导致大片地区干旱，土壤异常干燥，主要河流水位下降。预报员警告说，厄尔尼诺现象的加剧可能在今年晚些时候进一步推高全球气温。

body.en:
Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.

Western Europe experienced its hottest June and July on record , according to data released Monday by the EU's Copernicus Climate Change Service.

The average temperature across the region for the two-month period reached 21.62 degrees Celsius (70.92 Fahrenheit), breaking the previous record set in 2022.

Copernicus said the figure reflected the "exceptional persistence of heat" in western Europe, where four heatwaves have occurred since May.

The extreme temperatures have contributed to prolonged drought, major wildfires and new national temperature records across the region, as well as thousands of projected heat-related deaths.

Europe is the fastest-warming continent in the world, though temperatures varied considerably, with eastern Europe and Scandinavia experiencing much cooler conditions. For Europe as a whole, July was only the 11th warmest on record, with an average temperature of 20.49 degrees Celsius (68.88 Fahrenheit).

Conditions were drier than average across large parts of Europe in July, including Spain and other areas of the Iberian Peninsula, France , Germany , Austria , Hungary and the United Kingdom .

Ireland and parts of Iceland also experienced unusually dry conditions. Soil moisture in western Europe was significantly lower than in July 2022, when the region last experienced a severe drought.

"Persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over western Europe, the extreme temperatures also amplified widespread drought," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates Copernicus.

"As soils dry out, they lose their ability to provide natural cooling, allowing heat to build more readily," she added.

"This is a clear example of how climate change is intensifying heat extremes, with heat and drought increasingly reinforcing one another."

River flows were also unusually low , with the Seine, Rhine and Danube among the hardest-hit waterways. Low water levels have disrupted transport, irrigation and energy production in several European countries.

The hot and dry conditions have also increased the risk of wildfires. France and Spain have battled particularly severe fires this summer, while serious blazes have also hit other parts of Europe, the northwestern United States and Canada .

The average temperature across oceans outside the polar regions reached 20.96 degrees Celsius (69.73 Fahrenheit), surpassing the previous July record of 20.89 degrees (69.60 Fahrenheit) set in 2023.

body.zh: 欧洲大部分地区正遭受干旱，土壤异常干燥，主要河流水位下降。厄尔尼诺现象的加强可能会导致今年晚些时候全球气温进一步升高。 根据欧盟哥白尼气候变化服务机构周一发布的数据，西欧经历了有记录以来最热的六月和七月。 该地区两个月的平均气温达到21.62摄氏度（70.92华氏度），打破了2022年创下的纪录。 哥白尼表示，这一数字反映了西欧“异常持续的高温”，自五月份以来，该地区已经发生了四次热浪。 极端气温导致该地区出现长期干旱、重大野火和新的全国气温记录，预计还会造成数千人因高温而死亡。 欧洲是世界上变暖最快的大陆，尽管气温差异很大，东欧和斯堪的纳维亚半岛的气候要凉爽得多。对于整个欧洲来说，7 月只是有记录以来第 11 个最热的月份，平均气温为 20.49 摄氏度（68.88 华氏度）。 7月份欧洲大部分地区的天气状况比平均水平干燥，包括西班牙和伊比利亚半岛的其他地区、法国、德国、奥地利、匈牙利和英国。 爱尔兰和冰岛部分地区也经历了异常干燥的天气。西欧的土壤湿度明显低于该地区上次经历严重干旱的 2022 年 7 月。 欧洲中期天气预报中心气候战略负责人萨曼莎·伯吉斯（Samantha Burgess）表示：“持续的高压系统将热量困在西欧，极端的气温也加剧了大范围的干旱。”该中心运营着哥白尼。 “当土壤变干时，它们就会失去提供自然冷却的能力，从而更容易产生热量，”她补充道。 “这是气候变化如何加剧极端高温的一个明显例子，高温和干旱日益加剧。” 河流流量也异常低，其中塞纳河、莱茵河和多瑙河是受灾最严重的水道。低水位扰乱了几个欧洲国家的交通、灌溉和能源生产。 炎热干燥的环境也增加了发生野火的风险。今年夏天，法国和西班牙遭遇了特别严重的火灾，欧洲其他地区、美国西北部和加拿大也遭遇了严重火灾。 极地地区以外的海洋平均气温达到20.96摄氏度（69.73华氏度），超过了2023年7月创下的20.89度（69.60华氏度）的纪录。 大西洋沿岸部分地区和......测得创纪录的气温

title.en: Residents warned to brace for the worst as Canada wildfire rages out of control
title.zh: 加拿大野火失控，居民被警告做好最坏打算

summary.en: The Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia, still considered "out of control", has spread over 53 sq miles (136 sq km).
summary.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省的秃岭野火仍处于“失控”状态，已蔓延超过53平方英里（136平方公里）。

body.en:
A state of emergency has been declared after thousands of people were forced to flee their homes as a fast-moving wildfire spread rapidly in western Canada, doubling in size since it was first detected on Friday.

Police said one person has died in the Bald Range fire, which is burning across 53 sq miles (136 sq km) in Summerland and other areas of British Columbia, according to the BC Wildfire Service.

"We have to brace ourselves for the worst," Summerland Mayor Doug Holmes told Reuters. The Summerland area has been forced to evacuate along with thousands of others in nearby communities.

Officials said flames were so high they had created their own weather systems , which creates lightning.

Canadian police said on Sunday an 80-year-old woman from Meadow Valley, north-west of Summerland, had died suddenly while attempting to flee her home along with a member of her family. "Police believe her death to be a result of the wildfire," police said in a statement.

Keegan Radomski who lives in Summerland said she evacuated her home just moments before the fire reached her property.

In a video she shared with the BBC, burning tree tops are seen just over the hill beyond the road where Radomski made her escape.

Radomski said she has been unable to return since she fled with seven others on Friday. Now they're anxiously waiting on word whether they will still have a home to return to. She said some neighbours who stayed behind have reported many homes on their street burned down.

"There are homes that have been confirmed gone, and a lot are in the area near our home. So, we're pretty scared," she said. "The uncertainty is scary."

Residents that spoke to the BBC described the wildfire as one that intensified dramatically with little warning before it reached its current size of 13,618 hectares , external (33,650 acres).

British Columbia Premier David Eby told a news conference on Saturday that one fire official had likened the fire to "a bomb going off".

"Homes have been lost, and properties have been destroyed. Some people became trapped as conditions changed very quickly, and needed to be rescued," the premier said.

A state of emergency allows the provincial government access to special powers including travel restrictions and supply protections to prevent price gouging, and extra resources to coordinate rescue work.

Summerland, which has a population of about 12,000 people, has been one of the hardest hit areas and forced to evacuate. So were residents in parts of Peachland, which is home to about 6,500 residents.

"We have been on evacuation alert many times," said Earl Kurz, a Peachland resident of 30 years. "This is the first time we were actually evacuated."

body.zh: 由于一场快速蔓延的野火在加拿大西部迅速蔓延，自周五首次发现以来，火势扩大了一倍，数千人被迫逃离家园，加拿大宣布进入紧急状态。 据不列颠哥伦比亚省野火服务中心称，Bald Range 大火目前覆盖萨默兰、皮奇兰和不列颠哥伦比亚省其他地区超过 53 平方英里（136 平方公里）。 萨默兰市长道格·霍姆斯对路透社表示：“我们必须做好最坏的打算。”整个萨默兰地区以及附近社区的数千人都被迫撤离。 官员们表示，火势如此之高，以至于他们创建了自己的天气系统，从而产生了闪电。 住在萨默兰的基根·拉多姆斯基 (Keegan Radomski) 表示，就在大火蔓延到她家之前，她撤离了家。 在她与英国广播公司分享的一段视频中，可以看到拉多姆斯基逃跑的道路对面的山上有燃烧的树顶。 拉多姆斯基说，自从周五与其他七人一起逃离以来，她一直无法返回。现在他们正在焦急地等待消息，看看他们是否还有家可回。她说，一些留下来的邻居报告说，他们街上的许多房屋被烧毁。 “已经确认有些房屋已经消失，其中很多都在我们家附近。所以，我们非常害怕，”她说。 “不确定性令人恐惧。” 接受 BBC 采访的居民称，这场野火在没有任何预警的情况下急剧加剧，最终蔓延到目前 13,618 公顷的外部面积（33,650 英亩）。 不列颠哥伦比亚省省长大卫·伊比在周六的新闻发布会上表示，一名消防官员将火灾比作“炸弹爆炸”。 “房屋被毁，财产被毁。由于情况变化很快，一些人被困，需要救援，”总理说。 紧急状态允许省政府获得特殊权力，包括旅行限制和供应保护以防止哄抬物价，以及额外资源来协调救援工作。 人口约1.2万人的萨默兰一直是受灾最严重的地区之一，被迫撤离。皮奇兰部分地区的居民也是如此，该地区约有 6,500 名居民。 “我们已经多次处于疏散警报状态，”在皮奇兰居住了 30 年的厄尔·库兹 (Earl Kurz) 说。 “这是我们第一次真正被疏散。” 周五下午，库尔兹和妻子在奥肯纳根湖乘船，当时他看到清澈的蓝色天空迅速变成朦胧的灰色。夜幕降临时，熊熊大火上空的浓烟映入眼帘。它朝着库尔兹方向驶去。 几个小时后，警察敲开了他的门，命令他和他的妻子撤离。 秃岭野火引发了最大的...

title.en: Netanyahu rejects Trump-backed Gaza peace plan
title.zh: 内塔尼亚胡拒绝特朗普支持的加沙和平计划

summary.en: The Israeli prime minister has rejected a US-backed peace plan for Gaza, stating that Israel will not withdraw until Hamas is fully disarmed. This position puts him at odds with the proposed roadmap, which Hamas had endorsed.
summary.zh: 以色列总理拒绝了一项由美国支持的加沙和平计划，他表示以色列不会撤出加沙，直到哈马斯完全解除武装。这一立场使他与哈马斯已表示支持的路线图产生分歧。

body.en:
The Israeli prime minister says his country will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas fully disarms, putting him at odds with a US-backed roadmap endorsed by the group.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected US President Donald Trump's  plan for Gaza , saying Israeli troops would not withdraw from the territory until Hamas  was fully disarmed.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu told a Cabinet meeting, referring to the US-backed roadmap agreed to by Hamas in late July.

The Israeli military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed," Netanyahu said, adding that this included "heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry."

Netanyahu said Israel remained in talks with Washington despite its objections. He described Trump as "our greatest friend in the White House," but added: "They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters."

Trump announced last month that there had been a breakthrough on a 15-point roadmap aimed at ending the war in the Gaza Strip.

The plan drawn up by his Board of Peace calls for Israeli troops to withdraw as Hamas gives up its weapons. An International Stabilization Force would then work alongside a new Palestinian police force to secure Gaza.

Hamas is designated as a terrorist organization by Israel, the United States , the European Union and several other countries.

The group has avoided using the term "disarmament." It says it agreed to hand over its weapons for storage under a US-backed Palestinian technocratic administration that would govern Gaza under the supervision of the Board of Peace.

Hamas has said implementation also depends on Israel meeting its obligations , including withdrawing troops and halting attacks.

"We expect the mediators and the American guarantor to pressure Netanyahu and his government to adhere to the roadmap, and not obstruct the process for internal political and electoral reasons," Hamas political bureau member Bassem Naim said.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, said Israel would face no obligations until Hamas had surrendered all its weapons, including assault rifles.

However, Mladenov told Israel's Channel 12 that Israeli troops would eventually have to withdraw "sector by sector" once Hamas' weapons had been collected and rendered unusable.

"The option we are offering today is the only way forward that ensures this tragedy does not happen again," he said, referring to the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, which triggered the war against Hamas in the Gaza Strip.

Mladenov said discussions with Israel were continuing and that he hoped for a "positive outcome."

title.en: Evidence that South African special forces murdered top detective shared with BBC
title.zh: 南非特种部队谋杀高级侦探的证据与BBC分享

summary.en: Evidence has been shared with the BBC regarding the murder of top detective Frans Mathipa, who was shot while driving. The BBC gained access to the prosecution case against eight men accused in connection with his death, including members of South African special forces.
summary.zh: 英国广播公司（BBC）获得了针对八名涉案人员的起诉书，其中包括南非特种部队成员，这些证据与高级侦探弗朗斯·马蒂帕驾车时被枪杀的案件有关。

body.en:
Senior police detective Frans Mathipa had been fighting for four months to gain access to a crucial piece of information in the case he was working on. Finally, he was told, it was going to come his way.

Two days later, his car was found overturned - he had been shot dead while driving.

Now seven members of South Africa's special forces, and one military police officer, have been charged with murdering Lt Col Mathipa, a highly respected officer, in August 2023. They deny the charges.

There has been no date scheduled for their trial, and there are concerns it will never go ahead, because three of the men charged with his murder have refused to comply with a court order revoking their bail. They are still working for the army's special forces, and one of them has been promoted.

The BBC World Service has been given exclusive access to the prosecution case against all the men.

The case has caused consternation in one of Africa's most robust democracies, with fears the country's military is significantly overreaching its mandate.

We asked the South African army whether it was responsible for Mathipa's killing. It did not respond.

Several hundred pages of secret police and court documents, shared with the BBC, set out the evidence suggesting special forces killed Mathipa - who worked for an elite police unit known as "The Hawks".

We have also interviewed key sources in the police investigation - South Africa's former head of counter-terrorism in The Hawks; Mathipa's commanding officer; and Mathipa's family - to build the most comprehensive public account of the events leading up to the detective's death.

It presents a compelling case that South Africa's special forces are responsible for his murder.

In particular, police documents show that the vehicle that trailed Mathipa just before he was shot was registered to a front company for the special forces. And that tracking data found in that vehicle puts it at the scene of the shooting.

One of the men in the car, Maj Sunnybooi Wambi, the documents show, was also spotted at the scene of an alleged abduction carried out by special forces soldiers - the case that Mathipa had been investigating.

After Mathipa's death, special forces issued a chilling warning to The Hawks, the police documents say. "You can appoint 10 investigating officers; we will kill all of them," said the warning, according to police.

It centred on an Ethiopian man called Abdella Abadigga, an alleged so-called Islamic State [IS] militant. He had been granted temporary asylum in South Africa in 2008, but was arrested abroad in 2017.

Abadigga had then been smuggled back into the country, by the South African military and Department of Home Affairs, to be used as an intelligence asset - but had "gone rogue", according to Col...
body.zh: 高级警探弗兰斯·马蒂帕 (Frans Mathipa) 奋战了四个月，才获得了他正在处理的案件中的一条关键信息。最后，他被告知，这一切将会如他所愿。 两天后，他的车被发现翻倒了——他在开车时被枪杀。 现在，七名南非特种部队成员和一名宪兵被指控于 2023 年 8 月谋杀了德高望重的军官马蒂帕中校。他们否认了这些指控。 目前还没有安排审判日期，人们担心审判永远不会进行，因为被指控谋杀的三名男子拒绝遵守法院撤销保释的命令。他们仍在陆军特种部队工作，其中一名已经晋升。 BBC 世界频道已获得独家报道针对所有男子的起诉案件。 此案在非洲最强大的民主国家之一引起了恐慌，人们担心该国军队严重超越其职权。 我们询问南非军队是否对马蒂帕被杀负有责任。它没有回应。 与英国广播公司分享的数百页秘密警察和法庭文件列出了特种部队杀害马蒂帕的证据——马蒂帕为一支名为“鹰队”的精锐警察部队工作。 我们还采访了警方调查的关键消息人士——南非前鹰派反恐负责人；马蒂帕的指挥官；和马蒂帕的家人 - 建立关于导致侦探死亡的事件的最全面的公共账户。 它提供了一个令人信服的案例，证明南非特种部队应对他的谋杀负责。 特别是，警方文件显示，在马蒂帕被枪杀前跟踪他的车辆是在特种部队的一家幌子公司注册的。在那辆车上发现的跟踪数据表明它位于枪击现场。 文件显示，车内的一名男子桑尼布伊·万比少校也被发现出现在特种部队士兵涉嫌绑架的现场——马蒂帕一直在调查这一案件。 警方文件称，马蒂帕死后，特种部队向老鹰队发出了令人心寒的警告。据警方称，警告称：“你可以任命 10 名调查人员；我们将把他们全部杀死。” 它以一名名叫阿卜杜拉·阿巴迪加 (Abdella Abadigga) 的埃塞俄比亚男子为中心，他被指控为所谓的伊斯兰国武装分子。他于2008年在南非获得临时庇护，但于2017年在国外被捕。 随后，阿巴迪加被南非军方和内政部偷运回南非，用作情报资产，但据上校称，阿巴迪加已经“失控”。

reflection.en: When those entrusted with upholding the law are accused of its gravest violation, it highlights a profound breakdown in the justice system. Habakkuk's lament reminds us of the pain when the law is paralyzed and justice seems perverted, calling us to seek Yahweh's intervention for righteousness to prevail.
reflection.zh: 当那些受托维护法律的人被指控犯下最严重的违法行为时，这凸显了司法系统的深刻崩溃。哈巴谷的哀叹提醒我们，当法律瘫痪、公义似乎被扭曲时，那种痛苦是何等深重，这呼唤我们寻求雅伟的干预，使公义得以伸张。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.en: When nations face a "gulf" in worldviews, the path to peace can seem daunting. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. This calls for wisdom and perseverance in navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: How Kinahan's hearing unfolded inside the courtroom in Dublin
title.zh: 基纳汉在都柏林法庭受审的经过

summary.en: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan appeared in court in Dublin and was charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation after being extradited from Dubai.
summary.zh: 涉嫌犯罪头目丹尼尔·基纳汉在从迪拜引渡后，在都柏林出庭受审，被控指挥犯罪组织的活动。

body.en:
Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan appeared in court in Dublin on Sunday after being extradited from Dubai following his arrest there in April.

Kinahan has been charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.

The 49-year-old was remanded in custody after appearing at the non-jury Special Criminal Court in Dublin, telling the court: " I think we all know I won't be getting bail."

The Kinahan cartel has been responsible for trafficking tonnes of drugs and firearms around the world for more than 20 years, according to the UK's National Crime Agency.

The BBC's Ireland correspondent, Chris Page, was inside the court during the hearing.
body.zh: 犯罪头目嫌疑人丹尼尔·基纳汉 (Daniel Kinahan) 于四月在迪拜被捕后被引渡，周日出庭。 基纳汉被指控在 2015 年 10 月至 2017 年 4 月期间指挥犯罪组织的活动。 这位 49 岁的男子在都柏林无陪审团特别刑事法庭出庭后被还押，他告诉法庭：“我想我们都知道我不会获得保释。” 据英国国家犯罪局称，20 多年来，基纳汉贩毒集团一直在世界各地贩运大量毒品和枪支。 BBC驻爱尔兰记者克里斯·佩奇(Chris Page)在听证会期间在法庭内。

reflection.en: The appearance of a suspected crime boss in court underscores the enduring principle that governing authorities are established to uphold justice and maintain order. Even when justice is delayed, the legal process aims to hold individuals accountable for their actions, reflecting Yahweh's design for societal governance.
reflection.zh: 涉嫌犯罪头目出庭受审，强调了政府当局为维护正义和秩序而设立的持久原则。即使正义迟到，法律程序也旨在追究个人行为的责任，这反映了雅伟对社会治理的旨意。

verse.textEn: Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established.
verse.textZh: 在上有权柄的，人人当顺服他，因为没有权柄不是出于神的。

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

reflection.en: As Typhoon Dolphin forces evacuations and causes widespread disruption, we are reminded of our vulnerability in the face of nature's power. In such moments of crisis, Yahweh remains our steadfast refuge and strength, a constant help when trouble strikes. May those affected find safety and comfort in His presence amidst the storm.
reflection.zh: 当台风“海豚”迫使人们撤离并造成大范围破坏时，我们被提醒在自然力量面前的脆弱。在这样的危机时刻，雅伟仍然是我们坚定的避难所和力量，在患难中随时帮助我们。愿受影响的人们在风暴中，在祂的同在中找到安全和安慰。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.

title.en: Australia: Jetstar, Qatar Airways planes almost collide on Sydney Airport tarmac
title.zh: 澳大利亚：捷星航空和卡塔尔航空飞机在悉尼机场停机坪险些相撞

summary.en: A flight crew member was injured in a near-miss collision between two planes on the tarmac at Sydney Airport in Australia. An investigation has been launched to determine the cause of the incident.
summary.zh: 在澳大利亚悉尼机场的停机坪上，两架飞机险些相撞，一名机组人员受伤。目前已启动调查，以确定事故原因。

body.en:
A flight crew member was injured in a near-miss collision on the runway at Australia's Sydney Airport. An investigation has been launched to determine what caused the incident.

Two passenger aircraft —  a Jetstar and a Qatar Airways plane —  came close to crashing into each other on the tarmac at Australia's   busiest Sydney Airport on Sunday.

A crew member was injured and the incident has triggered a probe by the country's safety regulators.

The Jetstar A320 was taxiing for takeoff to the Gold Coast in the state of Queensland when its flight crew saw the Qatar Airways Boeing 777 —  which was being towed by an aircraft tug —  in close proximity on a crossing taxiway, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said in a statement.

"Both aircraft were stopped abruptly", the statement said, leading to a Jestar cabin crew member moving through the cabin being injured and the connection between the 777 nose gear and aircraft tug suffering damage.

The ATSB said that investigators were gathering data from both the planes, air traffic control, and interviewing crew and tug operators to determine the cause of the near collision.

The regulator put out a call for witnesses at the airport to send in any visuals of the incident.

Jetstar —  which is a low-cost subsidiary of  Australia's national carrier Qantas — said it was also conducting its own investigation.

"Our aircraft was following ⁠instructions ​by Air Traffic Control when the ​pilots were forced to brake firmly after another aircraft came in ​close proximity," a ‌Jetstar spokesperson said.

There was no immediate statement from Qatar Airways, which is the flag carrier of Qatar.

Meanwhile, flights at Sydney Airport were experiencing delays following the incident, government agency Airservices Australia said.

Sunday's incident ⁠comes a day after Sydney Airport witnessed widespread delays ⁠sparked by Airservices Australia authorizing  "departure spacing" due to roster issues with air traffic controllers.

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall, bringing strong winds and heavy rain across eastern China including Shanghai.

body.en:
Chinese authorities have evacuated more than a million people from their homes in eastern China including the financial capital Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall.

The typhoon brought heavy rain and halted transportation across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai alone on Monday.

While authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm, they continue to warn of torrential rains, severe flooding and the risk of landslides through to Wednesday as the storm moves north.

Chinese authorities had earlier issued their highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit China this year.

It packed maximum wind speeds of 150km/h (94mph) when it first slammed into Yuhuan in the Zhejiang province at 17:30 (09:30 GMT) on Sunday before making a second landfall in the city of Wenzhou about an hour later, meteorological authorities said.

Heavy rain was forecast on Monday for the provinces of Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and the city of Shanghai.

Governments have urged people to avoid outdoor activities, while several top tourist attractions remain closed, including parts of Disneyland and Legoland, and several viewing platforms along the Bund in Shanghai.

Footage on state media show ground-floor businesses flooded in the former French Concession in Shanghai, an area popular with tourists, and people wading through ankle-deep waters.

Several state media outlets have reported that a nine-year-old boy from Wenling, Zhejiang is missing after being swept into the sea. Chinese officials have not reported any casualties.

Parts of Zhejiang could receive 250mm to 500mm of rain over the next few days, forecasters say.

Authorities in Hangzhou, Zhejiang's capital city, have waived parking fees in all public spaces for drivers seeking shelter amid the strong winds and floodwaters.

Elsewhere in the province, Wenzhou authorities have relocated some 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters, while about 390,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in the city of Taizhou.

In the coastal province of Fujian, maritime authorities have suspended dozens of passenger ferry routes and halted more than 100 offshore construction projects.

The storm moved over a long distance of 6,000km before making landfall, suggesting a lifespan of more than three times that of an average typhoon, according to China's state broadcaster CCTV.

It also has a massive circulation size and intense rainfall capacity, CCTV reported.

Misinformation around the storm has apparently spread rapidly on the Chinese internet, with state media reporting that two people have been detained for distributing such content.

title.en: China: Typhoon Dolphin prompts mass evacuation, canceled flights
title.zh: 中国：台风海豚引发大规模疏散，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin is causing significant disruption across China, leading to the cancellation of nearly 1,500 flights in Shanghai and flood alerts in parts of Beijing, even as the storm begins to weaken.
summary.zh: 台风海豚正在中国各地造成严重破坏，尽管风力减弱，上海仍有近1500个航班被取消，北京部分地区也发布了洪水警报。

body.en:
Even as it weakens, Typhoon Dolphin is disrupting life in China. Close to 1,500 flights have been canceled in Shanghai while parts of Beijing are under flood alert.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds prompted flood alerts and more than 1,000 flight cancellations across China on Monday, even as Typhoon Dolphin weakened.

China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issued its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning as the storm lost power after making landfall in China's Zhejiang Province on Sunday.

Despite the weaker storm, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China will continue to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities issued their most severe flash flood alert for parts of eastern and southern Zhejiang on Monday, state news broadcaster CCTV reported. 

Five districts in Beijing are also under red alerts for heavy rainfall on Monday, with risks of landslides and flooding.

The storm had already forced over 300,000 people in eastern China to preemptively relocate, while bringing heavy rainfall to northern Taiwan over the weekend. In Shanghai, authorities evacuated more than 30,000 people out of high-risk areas. Overall, some one million people have been told to seek shelter. 

Shanghai's two main passenger airports, Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport, canceled 943 flights between them for Monday, the airport authority said in a post online. That's a reduction of capacity by nearly 40%.

On Sunday, the two airports had cancelled nearly 1,500 flights, or about 60% of their scheduled travel, according to state media.

Public transport services in the city were also impacted, with several local trains suspended.

Zhejiang's Ningbo International Airport will resume flights midday on Monday but warned that some of the scheduled travel may still be delayed or canceled as the storm had "not yet completely dissipated."

China is dealing with Typhoon Dolphin just two weeks after Typhoon Noul struck its southern Guangdong province. Last month, Typhoon Maysak killed 11 people and injured over 300 in the central Hubei province.

Extreme weather systems are a common feature in China this time of the year, with typhoons leaving significant displacement , infrastructural damage and loss of lives. Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of such extreme weather have increased and will continue to rise amid climate change.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin batters Japan's Okinawa before bearing down on China
title.zh: 台风海豚袭击日本冲绳，随后逼近中国

summary.en: The storm has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured five people on the Japanese island.
summary.zh: 这场风暴已导致日本岛上至少44,000栋建筑断电，并造成五人受伤。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured at least five people after hitting Japan's Okinawa island on Saturday.

Flights to and from Okinawa's main airport - Naha International Airport - were cancelled as it closed on Friday as the storm arrived.

The storm had maximum wind speeds of 162km/h (101mph) on Saturday and has been categorised as a "very strong" typhoon by the Japan Meteorological Agency, which warned of high waves, storm surges and lightning strikes.

Dolphin is expected to make landfall on China's eastern coast late on Sunday or early on Monday. Authorities there have shut ports and schools ahead of its arrival.

The main areas in Japan affected by the typhoon are the islands of Okinawa and Amami in the far south-west of the country.

Five elderly people suffered non-life-threatening injuries, according to the Okinawan prefectural government. Three of them fell because of the strong winds, it said.

Japan's national broadcaster NHK reports numerous accounts of trees being toppled by strong winds throughout Nago city in Okinawa, while a car was found overturned and leaking oil in a parking lot.

In China, Zhejiang's Ningbo Lishe International Airport said it would stop its operations from 23:30 local time on Saturday (15:30 GMT) and suspend all flights on Sunday.

A coastal typhoon alert in Zhejiang has been raised to its highest level, and port and ferry services have been halted in the Chinese province.

In Hong Kong, its weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9C on Sunday as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city.

Typhoon season in the western Pacific typically occurs between May and October, when typhoons are considered more commonplace. This year is a strong El Niño year , which experts say means typhoons can grow to be more intense.

In an average year of 25 cyclones reaching tropical storm strength in the region, around three usually make landfall in Japan, according to the country's meteorological agency.

Some of these will be strong enough to be classified as typhoons – as was the case with Dolphin.

A typhoon is the term used for storms that form in the north-west Pacific, whereas a hurricane is the term used for storms that form in the Atlantic or eastern Pacific.
body.zh: 周六，台风“海豚”袭击日本冲绳岛后，已导致至少 44,000 座建筑物断电，并造成至少 5 人受伤。 由于风暴到来，冲绳主要机场那霸国际机场周五关闭，往返航班被取消。 周六，这场风暴的最大风速为 162 公里/小时（101 英里/小时），日本气象厅将其归类为“非常强”台风，并警告称会有巨浪、风暴潮和雷击。 预计海豚将于周日晚些时候或周一早些时候登陆中国东部沿海。那里的当局在其抵达前关闭了港口和学校。 日本受台风影响的主要地区是该国西南部的冲绳岛和奄美岛。 冲绳县政府称，五名老人受伤，没有生命危险。据称，其中三人因强风而倒下。 日本国家广播公司NHK报道称，冲绳名护市多处树木被强风吹倒，停车场内发现一辆汽车翻倒并漏油。 在中国，浙江宁波栎社国际机场表示将从当地时间周六23:30（格林威治标准时间15:30）开始停止运营，并于周日暂停所有航班。 浙江沿海台风警报已提升至最高级别，该省的港口和渡轮服务已停止。 西太平洋的台风季节通常发生在五月至十月之间，此时台风更为常见。今年是厄尔尼诺现象强烈的一年，专家表示，这意味着台风可能会变得更加强烈。 据日本气象厅称，该地区平均每年有 25 个达到热带风暴强度的气旋，其中约 3 个通常会在日本登陆。 其中一些强度足以被归类为台风——就像海豚的情况一样。 台风是在西北太平洋形成的风暴的术语，而飓风是在大西洋或东太平洋形成的风暴的术语。

reflection.en: As Typhoon Dolphin brings disruption and injury, communities face the immediate challenges of recovery. In such moments of hardship, Yahweh's word reminds us that suffering, when endured, can forge resilience and a deeper hope within us and our communities.
reflection.zh: 当台风海豚带来破坏和人员受伤时，社区面临着即时的恢复挑战。在这样的艰难时刻，雅伟的话语提醒我们，苦难若能忍受，便能在我们和我们的社区中锻造出韧性与更深的盼望。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: Albanese, Japan's PM and melons: Behind the revived row over podcast remark
title.zh: 日本首相阿尔巴尼斯和瓜：播客言论再度引发争吵的背后

body.en:
Opposition leader Angus Taylor has called on Anthony Albanese to personally apologise for remarks the prime minister made about two crown melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart.

The criticism follows an opinion piece by former Japanese ambassador to Australia Shingo Yamagami, published in The Australian on Monday, which criticised comments Albanese made during a podcast interview last month with comedian Nikki Osborne.

Albanese was discussing two crown melons gifted to him by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during his visit to Japan in May, gesturing near his chest as he spoke about the fruit, which he said was a "pretty strange" gift but ended up being "quite good".

Yamagami said the remarks failed to recognise the gift's cultural significance and risked undermining Australia’s close relationship with Japan.

He said crown melons are highly prized in Japan, and the fruit gifted to Albanese was carefully cultivated in a specialised greenhouse.

Yamagami also highlighted Takaichi's position as Japan's first female prime minister, noting she had previously faced derogatory comments about her gender, including from Chinese officials.

"The last thing she expected was to be so casually mocked by the trusted leader of Japan’s special strategic partner," Yamagami wrote.

During Albanese's appearance on the podcast, Osborne asked the prime minister what the "most crap gift you've ever received on an overseas jaunt" was.

Albanese said he'd received a gift recently that was "pretty strange that ended up being quite good", explaining that he'd been given was a melon from Takaichi during her visit to Australia in May.

Osborne responded by asking him how the Japanese leader got the fruit into Australia.

"Did she smuggle it?" the podcast host asked, gesturing toward her abdomen, joking that Takaichi could have said she was pregnant.

"I don't know, 'I got a couple of melons,'" Albanese replied, while smiling and making hand gestures that some critics have interpreted as an inappropriate reference to breasts.

Osborne then replied: "She brought two? She just came in looking like Pamela Anderson."

A widely shared Facebook post last month had falsely claimed that Albanese compared Takaichi's breasts to Anderson's.

The comments have sparked renewed controversy after Yamagami's commentary was published in the Australian on Monday. That article followed another opinion piece published late last month by the Japan Times — and subsequently republished by The Australian on 1 August — which accused Albanese of sexism over the incident.

Premier Peter Malinauskas says AI presents major opportunities, but warns unchecked development could pose risks to society and the future of work.

"We can choose to allow this industry to come to our country and evolve in a way that is unregulated and unchecked," he said.

"Or we can choose to set the agenda … to ensure that we use AI in a way that puts people first."

The inquiry is expected to begin in October and deliver its final report by 1 July 2027. It's expected to focus on the economic and social opportunities the technology provides for the state.

He said the royal commission would offer a chance "to make sure that we all benefit from the opportunities".

summary.en: Raising compulsory super could do the same job as raising interest rates — but the money is yours. So why aren't we talking about it?

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Every time the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) meets to discuss the cash rate, millions of Australians hold their breath, knowing the outcome could affect their mortgage repayments , savings and household budgets.

Some economists say there's another way to cool spending — one that builds your retirement savings instead of handing more money to the bank through higher interest rates.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is due to hand down its next cash rate decision on Tuesday. Financial markets and most economists expect the RBA to leave the cash rate unchanged as inflation continues to ease, although the board has indicated it remains focused on returning inflation to its 2 to 3 per cent target.

Cooling inflation means squeezing demand somewhere. While governments can also influence demand through fiscal policy, such as changing taxes or government spending, it's now largely the RBA's job to adjust the cash rate to make borrowing more expensive. Higher interest rates can also strengthen the Australian dollar , making imports cheaper and reducing the demand for exports.

But this design hits homeowners in Australia harder than it does in many other countries, economist Chris Richardson says.

"Because we haven't built enough homes, Australia has really high housing prices and a lot of debt around that. And our interest rates are tied to short-term interest rates. So when we fight inflation, it tends to fall more on the shoulders of mortgage holders than you see in most other nations," he tells SBS News.

Richardson believes there's another lever that could be used instead of or alongside the cash rate: superannuation. Lift compulsory super contributions temporarily, and households would have less money to spend, helping cool demand, he says.

The difference is where the money goes — not interest to a bank, but savings for your own retirement.

Supporters say it could spread the burden of fighting inflation beyond borrowers. Critics argue it would simply shift the costs elsewhere. Here's how the idea stacks up.

The super guarantee (SG) is the compulsory minimum share of wages employers pay into eligible workers' superannuation. It's climbed steadily for over a decade — from 9 per cent in 2014 to its legislated final rate of 12 per cent on 1 July 2025 — with the aim of giving Australians a more comfortable retirement.

In 2021, more than 25 million Australians shared information about their personal lives, families, and occupations as part of the Census of Population and Housing .

Data collected by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) painted a detailed picture of the nation's diversity.

Almost half of all Australians had a parent born overseas, and more than 400 languages were spoken , including over 180 Indigenous languages.

On Tuesday 11 August, people will again be asked to share information about their lives for the 2026 Census.

The questionnaire is compulsory for everyone in Australia on Census night, including international visitors, refugees and migrants.

Here are some of the most common Census myths and questions — and what an expert says about them.

Emily Walter, a Census national spokesperson at the ABS, said there are misconceptions that the Census is a test or graded assessment tool.

"This is a self-reported questionnaire ... so, the right answer is always what represents you the best and who you are," she told SBS Examines.

The more honestly people answered, the more accurately the data reflected Australia's population, she added.

"It's really important that we understand how our cultural makeup is changing and everyone's individual responses contribute to that ... [and] provides the opportunity for local services to be provided."

Information collected during the Census cannot be shared with police, immigration agents or any other government departments.

By law, personal information, including names and addresses, must be separated from other Census data.

After the Census, names can be retained for up to 18 months, and addresses for up to 36 months.

The ABS has spent years assessing the privacy, security and processing of its data, with all information collected during the Census protected under the Census and Statistics Act.

The Census is often referred to as a national headcount or a snapshot of the nation, but it's used to inform funding for essential services like schools, hospitals, libraries and public transportation.

Walter said people's responses influenced the location and availability of English classes for newly settled migrants, which "help them then build their language skills and support them through applying for jobs or driver's licences or all of the things that you need to support yourself".

She added that Census responses cannot be used to make a person attend English language classes.

The Census must be completed in English; however, information about the survey is available on the Census website in 26 languages.

summary.en: Experts say the neurotransmitter dopamine plays a role in more of our habits and behaviours than we might realise.

What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but are its effects always beneficial? Watch Insight episode Chasing Dopamine Tuesday 11 August 8.30pm on SBS or SBS On Demand.

When Glenn Peterson started on a higher dosage of medication to treat his Parkinson's disease symptoms, he didn't expect the consequences it would have.

"I'd see a horse race, and I'd want the thrill of it winning, and betting on it. I had constant thoughts of sex as well, which never entered my mind prior to that. I couldn't get rid of it."

The 73-year-old was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease eight years ago. He was taking a dopamine precursor medication — a drug the body converts to dopamine when it reaches the brain — to treat his symptoms. He was later prescribed a dopamine agonist as well to make treatment more effective.

While the brain converts dopamine precursors directly into dopamine, dopamine-agonist medications mimic dopamine by activating dopamine receptors in the brain.

When combined, these drugs help treat the motor symptoms of Parkinson's, a progressive brain disorder that damages dopamine-producing neurons, but research shows agonist drugs can cause the development of compulsive and addictive behaviours.

Glenn says when the dopamine-agonist medication was increased, he developed these behaviours.

Glenn's wife, Robyn, also noticed the change when he started getting up in the middle of the night for hours at a time.

"And it started to come out that he was playing games ... or he'd gamble on the poker machines on his iPad through the night or go onto porn sites."

Glenn couldn’t understand why his mind seemed to turn against him. But when he revealed the extent of his newly developed compulsive behaviours to Robyn, she remembered the doctors had warned them that taking dopamine-agonist medication could bring on these side-effects.

They spoke to Glenn's neurologist and decreased his dose, which put an end to the compulsive behaviours.

Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in the brain that is involved in several of the body's functions, including movement — and contributes to our motivation and reward systems.
